name: the-panels-window-dots-take-clicks
description:
The reporter's window dots do nothing on the floating sidebar. The messages themselves reach the window and act on it - AtriumSidebarOverlayBrowserTest.TheWindowButtonMessagesActOnTheWindow proves that - so the question is whether a click on the dot ever leaves the page. The panel is a child window built Activatable::kNo, and the parent carves a hole in its own caption region for this row that the panel has no equivalent of.

The reading is a log line the handler prints. It appears only if the click reached the page, the page's own handler ran, and the message crossed the bridge.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself
collapse, so the edge zone arms
the left window edge, where the reveal is armed
a wiggle inside the strip - a move that lands without crossing the boundary fires no mouseEntered

actions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar edge reveal opening at
actions.note: the gate: the panel is up, so the click below has something to land on
the slide finishes and the page lays its chrome row out

actions.expression: (() => { const d = document.querySelector('.sbtd .td.close'); if (!d) return 'no dot'; const r = d.getBoundingClientRect(); const vis = getComputedStyle(d.parentElement).display; return 'x=' + Math.round(r.left + r.width / 2) + ' y=' + Math.round(r.top + r.height / 2) + ' group=' + vis + ' floating=' + document.documentElement.classList.contains('atrium-sidebar-floating'); })()
actions.note: where the dot is in the page, and whether the group is shown at all

the leftmost dot, on coordinates the page reported rather than derived: the eval above puts its centre at 15,20 in page space, and the panel sits 8 points in and 8 down from a window whose content starts at y=30 in this VM.

assertions.label: the-dot-sent-its-message
assertions.desc: Red while the click never leaves the page. The handler is proven separately, so a miss here is the click, not the plumbing.
